featured_reviews.review_text:
My detailed review of DG RUPAREL college

Campus(4.5/5): It's a pretty good campus as the ground is good but gets worse during rainy season so be careful of that . A volleyball court which is good too. Pretty good greenery all over the campus.

Places to chill(3.5/5): total 3 places are there for a group to sit properly one is named as Sawali which is just beside junior college staff room another one is Rupangan which is on the other end of the ground which is decent in terms of chilling and the last one is the banyan tree which is near the back gate of the college . If anyone wishes to play games near these places beware as the watchmen comes to take your id card if he sees you playing .(Places to worry are Rupangan and Banyan tree , sawali is safe )

Attendance (4/5): Attendance they say is compulsory and all but don't listen to them they are just bluffing just try to attend maximum number of practicals and submissions on time even for 12th lecture Attendance is not there .

Facilities(2/5): Facilities are not so great here the toilets aren't well maintained for boys it's okay but for girls idk but I think it'll be not so good . Other than that the ground for playing and all yes you can play on the ground only after you get your id card and have to ask in the office if playing on ground is allowed or not just to be on the safer side the timings for that are 3-6 only in the afternoon(if you are not from the college sports team for those students) . Classrooms are below decent sometimes it's as the infrastructure and all the benches tables fans etc are really old .

Crowd(3/5): Everyone will have different crowd preferences and they can get their type of crowd for being frnds as all types of people are in the college as for the seniors my personal experience was that as long as you are profitable to them they are good to you once your purpose is done they won't recognise you and all so don't look up to them if you want to socialize be a volunteer during ganpati festival and all and then you can be with them if you want .

Faculty(1/5): Idk abt com and arts but for sci the faculty is not good as they don't care much abt students and are not cooperating might even make fun of you in cases to look cool and all for cs branch in jr college there are 3 teachers out of which 1 is very very good and also personally clears your doubts and all 2 is good but very strict abt things she clears your doubts helps you too but she is a bit strict and the 3rd one is the most hated as she doesn't know what she is doing a lot of times she seems clueless and teaching also not good

Festivals: No such things as festivals but there are days around dec I think which lasts for 5-6 different days like saree day tie day etc and no freshers for newcomers if you are hoping from college if you want freshers there is an unofficial one organised by student council which requires ₹1000 per person and tbh it's total waste of money they promise unlimited food but it finishes after the 3rd round and no trips from college side again unofficial trip by student council which requires around 17-18k per person

Boards perspective (4/5): Teachers manage your marks in the internals help you during practicals and if you manage to stay in their good looks you'll get out of marks in the internals just attend the practicals and clear all the submissions on time

Overall(3/5): a decent college if you want stress free attendance and internals during boards etc but if you want to live your college life like in the movies plzzz don't come in this college

Hi ... my name is Deepak Ghume, I recently enrolled in the Master Certificate in Data Science course and it has been a great learning experience so far. I completed my BA in Economics in 2024, and coming from a non-technical background, I was initially unsure about starting Data Science. But the way the course is structured made the transition smooth and comfortable.

I started the program on 22nd December 2025, and within a short span, I have already completed Python and SQL. The teaching approach focuses strongly on concepts first and then practical implementation, which really helps in understanding the logic behind everything rather than just memorizing syntax.

The syllabus is very comprehensive — covering Python, SQL, R, Power BI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and even advanced topics like Forecasting and NLP. The course duration is 3 months, and it is designed in a way that keeps the pace balanced while ensuring proper depth.

I would definitely recommend this course to anyone who wants to build a strong foundation in Data Science, especially students coming from non-technical backgrounds like mine.

This was my lunch today( on 9/10/2024), though it was prepared much before my lunch time with a view to post it on Google Maps, admittedly.
The above pic is of ' Pan - seared Tiger Prawns( though Americans call it Shrimp, irrespective of it's size)!
RECIPE:
Ingredients:
3 X Tiger Prawns ( Rs.250.00)
1 large potato that  was turned like a Château potato( but smaller in size than an actual Château potato) Rs.6.00,
1 large carrot that was turned( To turn carrots and potatoes is an art and skill that chefs develop by practice only) with a paring knife like u make for glazed Carrots - Rs.6.50
2 X baby corn  -   Rs 10.00
6 X button mushrooms - Rs 22.00
1 X large tomato for making a flower  - Rs 10.00
5 g Amul butter - Rs.6.50
5 ml of Virgin Olive oil  - Rs 15.00
Salt to taste - Rs.0.25
Cilantro  to garnish - Rs. 0.25
Cooking gas  - Rs.10.00 approx.
Chef's time and labour =  Rs.200.0.( I have taken it on a very low  scale).
Therefore, total cost of  the production of the above dish =  Rs.530.00 in a city like Mumbai.
Method:
1) Wash the Tiger prawns well under running tap water.
2) Make a slit at the back,  from down its head to the tail of the tiger prawn and remove the intestine entirely ( technically called de - veining).
3) Wash again and make it dry in clean and sterilised cloth.
4) Marinate the prawns in a mixture  of table salt, freshly squeezed lemon juice or lime juice( as the case may be) and set aside for an hour so and if u wish, sprinkle with Paprika powder or Kashmiri  Red chilli powder and crushed black pepper and dash of Tabasco sauce and   a dash of Worcestershire sauce( optional) and please do it in moderation.
5) Turn the potato, Carrot and boil it in salted water and keep aside and for mushrooms, no need to boil and can straightaway sauté in the same skillet or pan.
6) Make a flower out a bright red tomato or rather call it a ' Rosette' and squeeze out the pips and juice out of the tomato and neatly slice the pulp and keep aside , to be tossed in butter while searing the tiger prawns.
7) Use skillet or a heavy cooking pan heat it up  and add a  drizzle of Virgin Olive oil and start  grilling the Tiger Prawns to a beautiful nice  golden brown color and put knobs  of butter and turn with spatula as and when required.
8) Add your potatoes, carrots and button mushrooms and grill and add thinly sliced  tomato slices  and keep the pan covered for a while and turn the prawns upside down. Cooking for a long time will make the prawns rubbery and leathery.
9) Dish out nicely and garnish with sprigs of fresh Cilantro or picked  Parsley  and may be with a wedge of lemon or lime (optional).
1 0)  Enjoy your meal of Tiger Prawns with steamed rice or  buttered rice/ plain Pulao or Pilaff as per your likes and dislikes!
HAPPY COOKING AND HEALTHY  EATING!!!
Please note:
This is absolutely my version of cooking the Tiger Prawns.
Professional Chefs have their own style and recipes.
I don't want to argue with anybody.
I just shared a RECIPE that I know!
P. S:
The moment you put the Tiger Prawns onto the hot pan, the color of the Prawns turns into a deep orange red color because the Astaxanthin in the shells gets converted into Astacin due to the heat in the pan.It is an interesting phenomenon to be noted.

featured_reviews.name: Charvi Dedhia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hansraj Jivandas College of Education is truly one of the finest institutions for anyone who dreams of becoming a professional, confident, and compassionate teacher. My experience here has been nothing short of transformative. The college doesn’t just teach you how to teach it grooms you into an educator who can multitask, manage responsibilities, and carry yourself with professionalism and grace.

The faculty is absolutely fabulous. Every teacher is well-trained, supportive, and genuinely invested in our growth. They don’t just deliver lessons; they mentor, guide, and push us to bring out the best version of ourselves. Whether it’s Usha Borkar ma’am, Pallavi Talekar ma’am, Archana Katgeri ma’am, Karuna Sinha ma’am, Shrima Bannerjee ma’am or Vaishali Sawant ma’am, or any other member of the teaching and support staff each one of them contributes immensely to a warm, encouraging, and enriching learning environment.

The college atmosphere is fun, loving, and full of positivity. The internship journey, though challenging, is like a roller-coaster ride that teaches you real classroom skills, patience, adaptability, and the true essence of being a teacher. You come out of it stronger, sharper, and more confident.

A special mention must be made of our Principal, Dr. Geeta Shetty. She is the heart of the institution warm, kind, approachable, and inspiring. Her guidance feels like gold, and she leads the college with a beautiful balance of discipline and empathy.

If you are planning to pursue a B.Ed, I can wholeheartedly say that Hansraj Jivandas College of Education is the best choice you can make. It not only shapes you into a skilled educator but also into a better person. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Nayar
featured_reviews.review_text:
What should have been a review has become a eulogy, as I was just informed that Dr. Sampat is no more.

A great principal isn’t just a leader; they are a force. They shape minds, build character, and leave a mark so deep that even years later, their words echo in your heart.

Dr. Urmi Sampat was that kind of principal. She wasn’t just an educator,she was an institution.

I still remember my first day at H.J. College. She stood at the gate in a crisp cream saree, radiating authority yet warmth. “What’s your name?” she asked. “Namrata  , and I’m am going to be the topper this year,” I replied with pride. She just laughed and said, “Go and sit yourself inside.” That was Dr. Sampat, no fuss, no unnecessary praise, just straight to the point. But in that moment, she acknowledged me. And with her, an acknowledgment always meant something.

She had this aura about her,if she caught you in the corridor, you’d hold your breath. If you were exhaling, you wouldn’t dare inhale again until she passed. That was the kind of presence she had. But beneath that formidable exterior was someone who truly believed in her students.

I remember struggling in my psychology paper. She called me in and asked, “What the hell have you done?” I admitted, “I had a blackout.” She didn’t let me off easily. “I don’t believe in blackouts, but I believe in you,” she said. And that belief changed me. I promised her I wouldn’t let her down. And when I topped my methods, she awarded me the prestigious Miss H.J Title of the year. That moment shaped my future in ways I didn’t even realise at the time.

One of the greatest compliments I’ve ever received came from her:

Personally, I see a junior Dr. Urmi Sampat in Namrata.
That comparison still humbles me.

Everything she taught me stayed with me. From my first lesson at NPKT to my journey as a teacher at Arya Vidya Mandir Bandra, to moving to Dubai , her words have never left me. The discipline, the passion, the high standards,they are woven into the way I lead today.

I wish I had the chance to say goodbye. But in a way, someone like her never truly leaves. Somewhere, I know she’s making sure everyone arrives on time, does their job well, and carries themselves with the grace and dignity she expected of us all.

Dr. Sampat, you were the epitome of grace, excellence, and discipline. They don’t make them like you anymore. I treasured you, and I always will.
Yours truly,
Namrata Simon Nayar

featured_reviews.name: Shami Sayed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Avoid.

I studied B.Ed. here and it was a traumatic experience for me. I couldn't find a detail review about this place, so I will present a honest review.

Although the quality of teacher education in most institutes is pathetic, this is a terrible place to be in if one wants to become a good teacher. If you want to be a teacher who has empathy and kindness for children then this isn't a good place because you might be pushed to be otherwise.

Some points to keep in mind before taking admission here:
1. Most "teachers" are openly partial and discriminating. They get a FAT salary by the government and "train" those students who on average will get a paltry sum of salary and this perhaps give them a sense of excessive superiority. They are miserly tyrants as they will demand you to get their personal and unrelated errands (mazdoori) done for free. Don't know if the old principal who was unreachable to students except till the last day also treated them like that, but their nervousness infront of her betrayed a sign of incompetence.

2. In the name of discipline you will get to be treated as a slave. True discipline is about following the rules which is good but these people are not concerned about rules and openly flout it e.g. wrongly confining the original documents, forcing students to do things that they are not required to according to the actual curriculum they paid the fees for, and some of them won't bat an eye to give mean degrading remarks. They forget that there's a Constitution which has certain rules for state-funded institutes.

3. The NAAC grade is a joke which they got by accommodating the officers in an expensive Juhu hotel (as proudly but ignorantly revealed by one "teacher")

4. The senior clerk Aditi Nerurkar is a hateful mean bigot (and possibly a psychopath) who seems to have been given a free hand by the college to be as such.

5. Teaching skills before joining this course won't be much different after completing it, and of course it will be because what can you learn when people (most teachers) who don't have subject content knowledge nor could they understand education in so many years, lectures you for hours 6 days a week and makes you study from poor content ripped off online. But you can become a drama artist (or dancer) because that's what happens often on priority.

6. Internships are held like the horrible show of big boss contest without any checks and balances for how students behave towards each other, but it's of not much concern to them of course because it doesn't affect them. It's majorly a total waste of time and you'll get the same repetitive feedback so basically you aren't growing as a teacher.

The only "strong point" of this course is the class presentation / speech which is simply about blabbering stuffs. Sadly, there isn't any good that I find here except maybe punctuality and obediance? Not sure if this place has always been like that since 1969, if so then I can't imagine their contribution to society. Either way, I don't know why they always demand to be worshipped.

featured_reviews.name: Saddu Samant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mithibai College is known for its excellent academic programs and active cultural environment. The college offers courses in arts, commerce, and science, and it attracts students from all over India. It is also well known for its festivals, events, and opportunities for overall student development.

featured_reviews.name: Nilesh Gohil
featured_reviews.review_text: Over all a good college with great professional people working over staff and faculty.. The student crowd is well disciplined without any cheap mischief.. infrastructure of the college is well updated with lifts,doors and other technologies. It has a spacious campus. College has most engaging cultural events and blood donation camps.. if you plan for after school studies svkm will help you build your career with strong pillars

featured_reviews.name: Andrea Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: A college with the best interiors and really good teachers. Attendance is strict but overall a great college which will develop your overall personality and academics. Has an amazing library with an advanced search system and wide range of books. Good canteen with Veg food where many hang out, as well as a cake shop with pastries and snacks for quick bites.

featured_reviews.name: Ronak Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: The Mithibai college is centrally airconditioned. Education level is well maintained. Attendance of 75% is mandatory for each Terms respectively. For FYJC Commerce students.. can take chances in Gujarati quota, if he scored 88% and above in the SSC board exam; whereas 93% and above will surely get admission to the General Quota(academic year 2023-24). The college canteen is very good. Food is tasty and hygienic. More or less but you can expect Upper, Middle++ and Middle+ category of crowd here. Very good location of Vile Parle. Total 9 min (Skywalk+Normal)  from Vile Parle railway station.

featured_reviews.name: Tirtham Haria
featured_reviews.review_text: The college is one of the best for students to study and has a vast array of facilities. The college has a big canteen and is centrally air conditioned. The college has many colleges in side its building. The college on any day could be seen bustling with students involved in various co-curricular activities and attending lectures.

featured_reviews.name: Nilesh Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: Best and oldest college of Mumbai. Having lots of celebrities college and sports personalities.

featured_reviews.name: Chintan
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best college in Mumbai. Managment, Administration as well as Facilities are top notch. Infrastructure of the college is amazing which makes it better than other colleges in the city. Each and every classes are equipped with Air Conditioners and Smart Boards. Teaching as well as Non Teaching Staff Members are amazing. Crowd of college is also good and there is zero tolerance towards ragging. As college is autonomous, teachers have flexibility to make their own syllabus which benefits students and make them future ready. Overall Amazing Educational Institute.

featured_reviews.name: Malav Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the best colleges in Mumbai. Run by Sri Vile Parle Kelavani Mandal. It offers several courses across Commerce and Arts. The quality of campus and progress is top notch in the city. Attendance is pretty compulsory.
